reporting-org.narrative: Young Women Christian Association of South Sudan

title.narrative: The Young Women For Awareness, Agency, Advocacy and Accountability (YW4A) Programme

description.narrative: Strengthening the advocacy capacity of 27 women’s rights organizations (WROs) to amplify young women’s voices in Palestine, Egypt, Kenya, and South Sudan by 2025. Enhancing the leadership of 17,540 young women to effectively engage in collective action and decision-making in public, private, and civic spaces in Palestine, Egypt, Kenya, and South Sudan by 2025. Transforming social norms and practices of 22 faith-based organizations (FBOs) that constrain young women’s rights in Palestine, Egypt, Kenya, and South Sudan by 2025. Influence the adoption, amendment, withdrawal or effective utilization and implementation of 18 laws and policies towards promoting young women’s rights to leadership, participation and ending SGBV in Palestine, Egypt, Kenya and South Sudan by 2025.

name.narrative: Juba, Mundri, Yei, Terekeka and Yambio County

title.narrative: WRGE 5.2.2: (WRG049y) IO2 Strengthened individual leadership of 13,700 young women across the four countries

description.narrative: This indicator refers to the number of young women who are trained TOT and who experience changes in leadership skills, experiences and practices. Leadership roles are measured by capacity to apply different forms of leadership training (to peers), willingness to become role models, self-confidence and efficacy, planning and facilitation skills, public speaking, advocacy, willingness to engage in policy change and with actors in public and civic decision-making spaces, exercise of leadership roles in the community, women’s groups, CSOs and political spaces, mobilization of young women, networking.

title.narrative: WRGE 5.2.2 (WRG049y) # of young women who have gained awareness of their rights, deepened their understanding of women's rights issues, and the ability to generate support around a common cause.

description.narrative: This indicator refers to the number of young women who are trained TOT and who experience changes in leadership skills, experiences and practices.

comment.narrative: Before the RiseUp! Training of Trainers started, 22 Cohort 1 young women took part in the Young Women Leadership (YWL) assessment as to measure their leadership capacity. The YWL score presents the young women's current capacity following the three classifications: Experienced, Aspiring, and Starting. In South Sudan the majority of Cohort 1 were classified as "Experienced" leaders. A smaller proportion were in the "Aspiring" phase. The smallest group were in the "Starting" phase, lacking required conditions and community leadership experience. Marginalised young women followed a similar distribution pattern across these categories.
The Cohort 1 training target for 2021 was set at 26 young women.

Capacity building activities with young women in Y1 concerned: AS 2.1.1.1Rise-Up material adaptation and training for key personnel: Adapt and train key WROs personnel on Riseup material; AS 2.1.1.2 Training of YW in Cohort 1, mentorship and leadership training, Training on baseline data collectors AS 2.1.1.2 Data collection workshops, Participatory data analysis workshop AS 2.2.1.1 Trainings in the Feminist Consultation Methodology.

The total endline target for South Sudan hasnot changed following the MTR, and is set at3,000 young women. Based on the actualsachieved so far, to reach the endline targetin South Sudan at least 1,120 young womenshould be trained in RiseUp! during 2024.Despite facing administrative challenges thatcould hinder reaching the remaining target,the strategy is to focus on empoweringyoung women in post-secondary institutions,leveraging the controlled environment ofschools for effective engagement andempowerment. Due to the setback experienced in 2023, the YW4A program was transitioned to CAPaD. The target for YWCA was set to 0, and the target for 2024 was included in CAPaD's reporting.
Due to the setback experienced in 2023, the YW4A program was transitioned to CAPaD. The number of young women trained in South Sudan is reported in CAPaD reporting.
Cohort 1 and 2 young women will cascade RiseUp and train another cohort of 1585 young women (cohort 3).

In South Sudan, a total of 1,500 out of the 1,585 target young women participated in the RiseUp! Leadership training. This is slightly below target. Some of these participants also received training in digital advocacy to enable them to share their knowledge with their peers in the FEM spaces. These young women demonstrated their leadership abilities through the Feminist Consultation Methodology (FCM), engaging with government officials, faith leaders, and influencers in their communities and schools. They addressed crucial issues such as the gender based-violence and the anti- gender-based violence bill, and child marriages.
The target in 2022 was set to be 312 young women to be trained in RiseUp! Leadership through cascading by the young women cohort 1 ToT.

Under Pathway 2, the YW4A programme enhances the leadership skills of young women through training and creating opportunities for them to train others and exercise their leadership, and be involved in advocacy. Throughout 2022, 350 young women were trained on the RiseUp! Leadership curriculum. Some of these young women have also participated in other trainings, for instance on legal and digital advocacy. The YW4A programme partners participated in various advocacy and dialogue spaces during the year, ensuring the involvement and active participation of young women and WROs.In South Sudan the number of young women trained for the first time in RiseUp! in 2022 were 190 young women from Yambio and Mundri. Due to capacity and accountability challenges, YWCA South Sudan spent the greater part of the second half of the year working on these issues -which resulted in delays in submitting the funds disbursement request and consequently, completed the training of young women in Juba, Yei and Terekeka in 2023. In total 168 young women (cohort 2) were trained. Upon validation of the South Sudan data, we came across a mistake in the reporting of the 2022 actuals. A total of 350 instead of 150 YW were trained in RiseUp! during 2022. This has been adjusted accordingly.

title.narrative: WRGE 5.2.1 (WRG045, WRG047, WRG048) I01 Enhanced capacity of 16-28 WROs to amplify young women's voices

description.narrative: Under IO1 YW4A focuses on enhancing the organizational and advocacy capacity of a selected group of women's rights organizations. The programme also envisages amplifying young women’s voices by promoting that WROs provide space in their internal organisations for young women and establish internal inclusive processes and practices in decision-making, management, and programming. And by working with WROs to include, represent, hear, mentor, support, and prepare young women to take part in advocacy initiatives, link them to strategic decision-making forums, and scale-up local advocacy strategies

title.narrative: WRGE indicator 5.2.1 (WRG047): # of WROs with enhanced capacity to advance young women’s rights to bodily integrity and equal participation in decision-making.

description.narrative: Under IO1 YW4A focuses on enhancing the organisational and advocacy capacity of a selected group of women's rights organsations through providing training.

comment.narrative: In South Sudan, YW4A targets a total of 6 WROs under IO1. In Y1 the advocacy and organisational capacity of the participating WROs was measured, as to set the baseline situation. In South Sudan the WROs baseline AOCA capacity level is assessed as follows: 3 WROs at FAIR capacity (1 WRG047, 2 WRG045); 2 WROs at BASIC capacity (1 WRG045, 1 WRG048). One of the WROs was not yet active at the time of AOCA assessment, hence this organizations' baseline will be measured at a later stage.
One of the WROs opted out of the programme in the inception phase of YW4A; it's replacer was not yet active in 2021.

Capacity building activities with WROs in Y1 concerned: AS 1.1.1.1 Country inception meeting with WROs and FBO, AS 1.1.1.2 Capacity assessment inception meeting ( AOCA ) process, AS 1.1.1.3 Individual and collective assessment with WROs and FBO on advocacy and organizational capacity, AGT 13 /S Participatory design of M&E framework, AS 1.4.2.1 Legal and policy analysis, AS 1.1.1.7 General advocacy training, AS 1.1.1.8 Legal advocacy training
During 2023, YW4A continues to target the same WROs (those that take part from the start and replacing WROs).

Capacity building continued throughout 2023, not only through trainings, but also through coalition building and joint advocacy efforts. The results from the AOCA mid-term assessment show progress among all four WROs that were involved in YW4A since the start. At mid-term 2 WROs have moved up one level on the AOCA scale compared to baseline, and the other 2 WROs even moved up two levels. Hence in South Sudan, 100% of the WROs that joined YW4A since 2021 have met YW4A’s IO1 target to move up one level or more on the AOCA scale. At mid-term the AOCA capacity of the 5 involved WROs is: 1 LIMITED capacity, 1 BASIC capacity and 3 WROs at MODERATE capacity. While there are still limitations in the organisational capacity of some WROs, for example some of the organisations relied fully/largely on volunteers and internet connectivity is a hindering factor, one WRO indicated that as a result of YW4A participation they included young women in their decision-making body. Advocacy and legal training was also key for enhancing participants' knowledge of national and international laws as well as key advocacy priorities, including for their contributions to the ratification of the Maputo Protocol.
In 2022, YW4A is targeting the same 5 WROs as in 2021. A 6th WRO joined the programme as to replace the WRO that opted out in 2021.

Throughout 2022, YW4A partners undertook activities to build all WROs’ advocacy and organisational capacity. For example, through training on legal and digital advocacy the targeted WROs in South Sudan have increased their capacity. Building on legal capacity strengthening undertaken in the first year, partners have enhanced capacity to scale up the critical work they have been doing in addressing women’s rights issues and using their experiences to call for action from duty bearers through various advocacy initiatives in line with the YW4A advocacy priorities and the laws and policies targeted under IO4. They now have the required skills to supplement their legal advocacy campaigns with media strategies. This increased capacity to engage in legal advocacy can also be seen in the way WROs and young women are being strategic when engaging national processes and different policy makers and actors in their country. In South Sudan, six organisations targeted by YW4A (similar to Y1) took part in these activities. A new WRO joined YW4A at the beginning of 2022 as a replacement of the WRO that opted out of the programme in the inception phase of YW4A. Throughout the course of the year, two WROs became more and more inactive and the partner has started the process to replace these two WROs in 2023
During 2024, YW4A continues to target the same WROs (those that take part since the start and new WROs that replaced initial selected WROs).
